rfi.title: Culture versus climate: how global heating endangers Unesco heritage sites
rfi.description: Unesco World Heritage sites in France and around the world are under threat from the climate crisis. From ancient cities to medieval abbeys, floods, droughts, rising seas and wildfires are putting humanity’s most precious cultural heritage at risk.

rfi.title: More than half of Europe exposed to extreme heat stress this summer
rfi.description: A record 52 percent of the European continent was exposed to intense heat stress during the summer of 2026, according to the European Union’s Copernicus climate monitoring service. The season saw Europe experience four of its 10 worst heatwaves on record.

rfi.title: EU approves tougher migration rules in latest push to tighten borders
rfi.description: European Union interior ministers agreed on Thursday to toughen the bloc's migration policies, particularly on returns of undocumented migrants. They also want to step up social media monitoring to prevent further mass movements of people after the crisis in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta this summer.

rfi.title: From London to Les Bleus: Olise proves his potential in Zidane's new wave
rfi.description: On a cloudy night in Brussels, Michael Olise took nine seconds to highlight his genius and maintain the euphoria around France's new head coach Zinedine Zidane.

rfi.title: France launches €35m fund to attract private investment to overseas territories
rfi.description: France has launched a €35 million investment fund to attract private capital to businesses in its overseas territories, as the government seeks to shift the focus from subsidies towards growth, innovation and regional expansion.

rfi.title: Family feud yields sour grapes at French drinks empire Castel
rfi.description: A court in Singapore is preparing to rule on a power struggle at the Castel Group, a family-run French beverage business that has grown to be one of the largest drinks companies in Europe and Africa – and is currently the subject of a dispute between two of the founder's relatives and the CEO, the first person outside the Castel family to run the multibillion-euro business.

rfi.title: Nuremberg trials: 'When you see these people in the dock, the world changes'
rfi.description: The Nuremberg trials, held by the Allied powers after the Second World War to prosecute prominent Nazis for war crimes, came to an end on 1 October, 1946. The 10 months of hearings marked a turning point in international criminal justice, paving the way for the International Criminal Court. Bruno Cathala, who helped build the ICC, tells RFI how the Nuremberg trials changed the course of history.

rfi.title: Infantino loses Swiss backing for campaign to remain Fifa chief
rfi.description: Gianni Infantino's drive to remain boss at world football's governing body Fifa was under threat on Thursday after his own country's football association withdrew its support.

rfi.title: 'Catastrophic': Swiss glaciers lose fifth of mass in five years
rfi.description: Switzerland's glaciers, which are disproportionately impacted by climate change, have lost nearly 20 percent of their mass in five years, experts said Thursday, with 2026 registering the second-biggest melt on record.

rfi.title: Paris court jails six men for manslaughter over mass drowning in Channel

france24fr.description: Un deuxième grand pont de Kiev a été touché par des frappes russes en quelques jours. Après le pont Sud, visé jeudi et vendredi, le pont Nord a subi des dégâts samedi, notamment sur la chaussée et les câbles des trolleybus.

france24fr.title: Vol Flydubai : l'enquête émiratie établit que le copilote planifiait un "acte terroriste"
france24fr.description: Le copilote omanais accusé d’avoir poignardé son commandant de bord à bord d'un avion de Flydubai, le 30 septembre, a tenté de mener une attaque "terroriste" selon le procureur général des Émirats arabes unis. L’homme aurait attaqué le commandant de bord avec une hache de secours dans le cockpit et tenté de prendre le contrôle de l’appareil.

france24fr.title: La Corée du Nord tire un missile balistique en direction de la mer du Japon
france24fr.description: La Corée du Nord a effectué samedi matin un nouveau tir de missile depuis la région de Wonsan, sur sa côte est. Selon Séoul et Tokyo, le projectile, qui est tombé en mer à environ 700 km de son point de lancement, pourrait être un missile balistique. L’armée sud-coréenne a immédiatement renforcé sa surveillance et coordonné le suivi de la situation avec les États-Unis et le Japon.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : le décret-loi 54 assoupli, la peine de prison pour une première infraction disparaît
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, le décret 54, un texte promulgué par la Présidence de la République en 2022, a été amendé mercredi 30 septembre. Ce texte supposé lutté contre la diffusion de fausses informations et de rumeurs sur les réseaux sociaux a été surtout utilisé ces dernières années pour réprimer la liberté d'expression dans le pays

france24fr.title: Contestation lycéenne, récupération politique et budget : peut-on encore éviter le chaos?
france24fr.description: Cette semaine la contestation lycéenne a pris une ampleur nationale. Et cette colère arrive au pire moment pour le gouvernement puisqu’il vient de présenter son projet de budget pour 2027. Jusqu’où ira la crise ? On en parle avec Virginie Martin, politologue et professeure à Kedge Business School.

france24fr.title: "Costard en kevlar" : les rédactions de 39 médias condamnent les propos de M. Le Pen contre Mediapart
france24fr.description: Les sociétés de rédacteurs et de journalistes d'une quarantaine de médias français, dont France 24 et RFI, ont publié vendredi une tribune condamnant les récentes déclarations de la candidate à la présidentielle du Rassemblement national Marine Le Pen visant le site d'investigation Mediapart. Elles dénoncent de "violentes tentatives d'intimidation" contre la liberté de la presse, qu'elles jugent "particulièrement inquiétantes pour le droit à l'information auquel peut prétendre la population d'un

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ligue des nations : les Bleus tenus en échec par l'Italie pour la première de Zidane à domicile
Ligue des nations : les Bleus tenus en échec par l'Italie pour la première de Zidane à domicile
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France a été neutralisée par l'Italie (1-1), vendredi soir, en Ligue des nations au stade de France à Saint-Denis. Pour la première de Zinedine Zidane à domicile en tant que sélectionneur, les Bleus ont longtemps cru pouvoir l'emporter avant de céder face à la Squadra Azzurra et de se faire peur en terminant le match en infériorité numérique.

france24fr.title: Étudiante "blessée par des agresseurs", "personnel aspergé d'essence" : le gouvernement a menti ?
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la semaine, le mouvement de blocage des lycées prend de l'ampleur et de nombreuses images de violence y sont associées. L'occasion pour les responsables politiques de se livrer une bataille sur ce sujet. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a assuré qu'une étudiante avait été agressée. Le ministre de l'Éducation Nationale Edouard Geffray que des personnels avaient été aspergés d'essence. Est-ce vrai ? Décryptage dans Info Intox avec Jules BOITEAU.

france24fr.title: Clap de fin pour Cristiano Ronaldo ?
france24fr.description: Le Portugal a remporté, jeudi face au Danemark, son troisième match consécutif de Ligue des nations – les deux dernières rencontres ayant été gagnées sans la participation de Cristiano Ronaldo. Une sortie ratée de la part du quintuple Ballon d'or, qui a quitté le rassemblement mercredi soir.

france24fr.title: Brexit : "Trop gros, trop tôt" pour envisager un retour du Royaume-Uni au sein de l'UE
france24fr.description: Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit, l'hypothèse d'un rapprochement entre Londres et Bruxelles revient dans le débat politique britannique. Le Premier ministre Andy Burnham a même évoqué la possibilité d'une réintégration du Royaume-Uni au sein l'UE. Si la perspective d'un "Breturn" semble encore éloignée, "il y a certainement beaucoup mieux à faire que de maintenir le statu quo", estime Sébastien Maillard, conseiller spécial à l'Institut Jacques Delors.

france24fr.title: Vincent Duclert: "la dédiabolisation du RN a littéralement volé en éclats"
france24fr.description: La question de l'antisémitisme a percuté la campagne à la présidentielle, avec les révélations de Mediapart au sujet des écrits passés de Jordan Bardella. La dédiabolisation de l'extrême droite française n'était-elle qu'un leurre? Pourquoi cette persistance de l'antisémitisme au sein d'une partie de la classe politique et de la société française ? L'historien Vincent Duclert, auteur de "La philosophie contre l'antisémitisme" (éditions PUF), était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : face aux débordements, le maintien de l'ordre en question
france24fr.description: Depuis qu'il s'est élargi, le mouvement de protestation des lycéens est rythmé par de nombreux débordements. En réaction, la présence policière apparaît comme massive, et plusieurs manifestants dénoncent des faits de violences. Un climat tendu, attisé par l'assimilation du mouvement à des "violences urbaines", selon le spécialiste Olivier Cahn.

france24fr.title: Non, la police nationale n’a pas lâché un chien sur des lycéens à Lille
france24fr.description: Sur la base d’une vidéo circulant sur les réseaux sociaux, la police nationale a été accusée d’avoir lâché un chien sur les élèves qui avaient organisé mardi le blocus du lycée César Baggio, à Lille. Or, selon les journalistes qui couvraient l'événement, le chien visible dans la vidéo n'appartenait pas aux forces de l’ordre.

france24fr.title: Ghana : Carlos Queiroz démissionne après cinq mois sur le banc des Black Stars
france24fr.description: Carlos Queiroz a annoncé jeudi quitter son de sélectionneur du Ghana. Après seulement cinq mois sur le banc des Black Stars, l'entraîneur portugais paie notamment les résultats décevants de sa sélection.

france24fr.title: Jugé coupable de "graves" infractions financières, Manchester City fait appel
france24fr.description: Après avoir été jugé coupable de "graves" infractions financières, le club de Manchester City a annoncé vendredi avoir fait appel dans cette affaire aux "conséquences majeures pour l'intégrité" du jeu, selon la Fédération anglaise de football.

Proteste in Indien: »Der Teeverkäufer ist ein Dieb«
zeit.description: Die junge Kakerlaken-Bewegung hat die indische Demokratie wiederbelebt. Nun geht die Gen Z erneut auf die Straßen – und wird zum echten Problem für die Regierung.

Unfälle: Motorräder prallen zusammen - 54-Jähriger schwer verletzt
Angriff bei Flug nach Tel Aviv: Flydubai-Co-Pilot soll Terroranschlag geplant haben
zeit.description: Mit einem Beil soll der festgenommene Flydubai-Co-Pilot den Piloten angegriffen haben. Die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate sprechen von einem versuchten Terroranschlag.

nzz.title: Fundamentalisten auf dem Vormarsch: Wie jüdisch soll der jüdische Staat sein?
nzz.description: In Bnei Brak schimpft ein Säkularer über «irre Fanatiker», in Jerusalem wähnt sich ein Rabbiner bereits in einem «Religionskrieg»: In Israel schlittern Weltliche und Ultraorthodoxe immer tiefer in einen Konflikt, der von Ängsten und Untergangsphantasien geprägt ist.

nzz.title: Mutmassliche Gruppenvergewaltigung an der Cornell-Universität: «Ist der Laden noch offen?», fragt ein Elite-Uni-Student den anderen. Er meint nicht den Kiosk
nzz.description: Eine 20-jährige Studentin soll vor zwei Jahren von sieben Kommilitonen vergewaltigt worden sein, ohne dass es zu einer Strafverfolgung kam. Der Fall erzeugt solche Empörung, dass New Yorks Gouverneurin Kathy Hochul eine Sonderermittlerin einsetzt.

nzz.title: Westschweizer SVP-Chefs beanspruchen Parmelins Sitz im Bundesrat
nzz.description: Bundesrat Guy Parmelin soll von einem Romand ersetzt werden, fordern die Präsidenten der Kantonalparteien einhellig. Aber das ist alles andere als sicher.

nzz.title: Enttäuschung in Bern über die unnachgiebige Haltung der Schweizerischen Nationalbank
nzz.description: Die SNB hat ihre vorsichtige Gewinnausschüttungspolitik in harten Verhandlungen mit dem Eidgenössischen Finanzdepartement verteidigt – und nur Hand für eine marginale Änderung geboten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die verstörende Geschichte der Amerikanerin Christa Pike zeigt: Es gibt keine humane Todesstrafe
nzz.description: Die «death penalty» erlebt in den USA ein politisches Revival. Doch die extremste Form der Bestrafung scheitert an ihren eigenen Widersprüchen. Zeit, dieses Relikt abzuschaffen.

nzz.title: Unbekannte sollen in die Wohnungen von finnischen Parlamentariern eingedrungen sein – Präsident Alexander Stubb spricht von einem «Angriff auf die Demokratie»
nzz.description: Mysteriöse Einbrüche schrecken Finnland auf. Über die Täterschaft ist noch nichts bekannt – aber es gibt einen schlimmen Verdacht.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK MIT DATEN - Die Ostdeutschen sind wirtschaftlich nicht abgehängt
nzz.description: Die Kaufkraft der Bürger im Osten Deutschlands ist höher als in den meisten EU-Ländern. Das hat mehrere Gründe.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Stopfleber hat mir sogar geschmeckt», sagt die Frau, die Foie gras verbieten will
nzz.description: Katharina Büttiker von der Organisation Animal Trust hält nichts von dem Gegenvorschlag, mit dem das Parlament ihre Volksinitiative bodigen will. Die Tierschützerin sieht darin eine reine Beruhigungspille – und die Verschwendung von Steuergeldern.

nzz.title: Das Unwesen der eigenen Geschichte: Tschechien als Gastland an der Frankfurter Buchmesse
nzz.description: Die Schriftstellerinnen Radka Denemarková und Alice Horáčková erzählen in ihren Romanen von der schwierigen deutsch-tschechischen Vergangenheit – ganz unterschiedlich, aber äusserst lesenswert

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - «Wir müssen zeigen, dass Leute sterben» – Kriegsfotograf Dominic Nahr
nzz.description: Seit zwanzig Jahren fotografiert der NZZ-Fotograf Menschen in Krisengebieten. Im Podcast erzählt Dominic Nahr, wie er seine Arbeit machen kann, ohne sich selbst dabei zu verlieren.

nzz.title: Franz hat sich vor aller Welt zum Narren gemacht und daran erinnert, wie radikal die christliche Botschaft ist: Was man vom Mann aus Assisi lernen kann
nzz.description: Friedensstifter, Prediger der radikalen Armut, Ökologe avant la lettre: Franz von Assisi wird für vieles in Anspruch genommen. Auch für manches, was er nicht war. Vor 800 Jahren ist er gestorben.

nzz.title: Bananen werden dank Genmanipulation nicht mehr so schnell braun. Können sie damit auch vor dem Aussterben gerettet werden?
nzz.description: In England könnte bald eine Banane auf den Markt kommen, die mit der Genschere Crispr/Cas verändert wurde. Die Methode könnte auch helfen, die Frucht gegen einen tödlichen Pilz resistent zu machen.

nzz.title: Kriegsangst und russische Agenten: So versucht der Kreml die Wahlen in Lettland zu beeinflussen
nzz.description: Seit den neunziger Jahren nimmt Russland Einfluss auf die Politik in Lettland. Auch bei den Wahlen am Samstag stehen offen prorussische Parteien auf der Liste. Werden sie Erfolg haben?

nzz.title: Störungen in der Durchblutung des Gehirns könnten eine Ursache von Autismus sein
nzz.description: Bisher galt, dass ausschliesslich Defekte in Nervenzellen Autismus auslösen. Eine neue Studie widerspricht dem nun. Und die Forscher liefern sogar eine mögliche Therapie – mit Augentropfen.

nzz.title: Dieses Virus kann den Körper chronisch anfällig machen
nzz.description: Das Pfeiffersche Drüsenfieber hat manchmal langfristige Folgen. Viele Betroffene klagen anschliessend über häufigere Erkältungskrankheiten. Was Experten über das Phänomen herausgefunden haben. Die Kolumne «Hauptsache, gesund».

nzz.title: Eine Tunnelkatastrophe beschleunigt die Elektrifizierung des Schweizer Zugnetzes
nzz.description: Vor hundert Jahren sterben im Rickentunnel neun Menschen an einer Kohlenmonoxidvergiftung, bald danach schon sind Dampfloks in der Schweiz Geschichte.

observador.title: Efeitos no lobo ibérico pesam no chumbo de parque do Paiva
observador.description: Parque eólico proposto pela Lightsource BP previa a instalação de 45 aerogeradores em cinco concelhos dos distritos de Viseu e Guarda e colocava em risco proteção e recuperação da espécie protegida.

observador.title: 8h. Cuidados continuados registam prejuízo de 180 mil euros
observador.description: Os números são da Faculdade de Economia do Porto, que alerta para um sub-financiamento que pode ultrapassar os 6 mil e 600 euros por utente. Ainda, Frente Cívica questiona proteção de Rui Pinto.

observador.title: "O Caminho de Santiago dá-me energia"
observador.description: Miguel Costa realizou, este ano, o oitavo Caminho de Santiago: pedalou os 800 quilómetros do Caminho Francês que começa nos Pirinéus. É uma aventura que acaba de partilhar em livro.

observador.title: Operação Influencer: PGR diz que Costa não pode ver processo
observador.description: O esclarecimento surge após o semanário Expresso noticiar que MP recusou seis pedidos de Costa para consultar o inquérito. Ainda, em Espanha, inquilinos manifestam-se hoje contra os preços das rendas.

observador.title: 6h. MAI. César Boaventura apresenta participação contra PJ
observador.description: A queixa enviada à Procuradoria-Geral da República pede que sejam investigados crimes de peculato de uso e abuso de poder. Ainda, Ventura recusa que António Costa seja vitima na Operação Influencer.

observador.title: OpenAI adia modelo Astra após falhas de segurança nos testes
observador.description: OpenAI cancelou lançamento do novo modelo após perceber que a IA estava a fazer mais do que lhe era pedido nos testes e sem explicar como o fazia. Empresa resolveu dar passo atrás, mas não desiste.

observador.title: Brasil dividido: conseguirá Flávio Bolsonaro travar Lula?
observador.description: Bruno Cardoso Reis analisa as eleições no Brasil perante um mundo em ebulição: da ameaça nuclear de Putin em Kaliningrado à reaproximação britânica à UE e ainda o congelamento de armas a Taiwan.

observador.title: Canções que descobrimos em setembro
observador.description: Da pop à neo-soul passando pelo rock nacional e hip hop: de Beyoncé e Stevie Wonder a Glockenwise, Tiago Villhena e Espama Trincana, reunimos o mapa essencial das novidades que descobrimos este mês.

observador.title: Presidenciais no Brasil: uma primeira volta previsível?
observador.description: As sondagens mostram que Lula da Silva e Flávio Bolsonaro devem passar à segunda volta das presidenciais brasileiras. Mas poderá haver alguma surpresa? Pedro Benevides é o convidado.

observador.title: 4h. Governo não quer excluir médicos tarefeiros do SNS
observador.description: Ana Paula Martins manifesta disponibilidade para os integrar, mas de acordo com a legislação em vigor. Ainda, o Ministério da Defesa polaco está a redigir uma lei para preparar o país para a guerra.

observador.title: 3h. Homens iranianos acusados de terrorismo em Manchester
observador.description: Em causa, um plano que estariam a desenvolver para atacar a comunidade judaica em Manchester. Ainda, o Ministério da Saúde garante que não quer excluir os chamados médicos tarefeiros do SNS.

observador.title: 2h. Defesa da Polónia redige lei de preparação para guerra
observador.description: Esta lei pode incluir o destacamento de tropas para pontos considerados “sensíveis” dentro da NATO. Ainda, doações de oligarcas russos correspondem a mais de 1% do Orçamento do Estado da Rússia.

observador.title: 1h.  Flydubai. Suspeito tinha sido já afastado por companhia
observador.description: O suspeito do ataque à Flydubai já tinha sido afastado pela companhia aérea nacional de Omã. Ainda, Donald Trump não vai proibir as exportações de combustível para a Europa

observador.title: Manchester. Dois acusados de planear atentado contra judeus
observador.description: Dois homens têm origem iraniana, sendo um deles refugiado. Ministro veio relacionar ataque com imigração ilegal. Tinham construído bomba e pesquisado alvos.

observador.title: O caso das gémeas mostra a importância de um telefone no SNS
observador.description: Quem tiver nascido nas famílias certas, quem tiver estudado nas escolas certas, quem tiver os amigos certos e quem tiver entrado no partido certo, terá na agenda o número certo de telemóvel e salva-se

observador.title: O Ocidente que resistiu a bordo de um Boeing
observador.description: Os israelitas a bordo, com a indispensável ajuda do comandante, perceberam que ou tratavam do assunto ou o assunto trataria deles. Já haverá "activistas" a exigir a sua punição.

observador.title: O Cónego Jeremias e a laicidade do Estado
observador.description: A Constituição nunca diz que Portugal é um país laico, apenas que é não confessional. E não confessional não quer dizer laicista

observador.title: Igual ao mesmo
observador.description: Será que as coisas que vemos com os olhos abertos continuam a existir da mesma maneira quando os fechamos?

spiegel.title: Straße von Hormus: Unbekannte beschießen Tanker vor Oman
spiegel.description: In der für den weltweiten Energiehandel wichtigen Straße von Hormus sind zuletzt regelmäßig Schiffe angegriffen worden. Nun haben Geschosse einen Rohöltanker getroffen, nahe der Nordspitze Omans.

spiegel.title: Tag der Deutschen Einheit: Ostdeutschland bietet einen Blick in die Zukunft. Lernen wir daraus
spiegel.description: Die Wahlen in Ostdeutschland erschüttern die Politik. Dabei sind sie für die Parteien der Mitte auch eine Chance. Die Erfahrungen zeigen, wie man in Zeiten wachsender Polarisierung Menschen für sich gewinnt.

spiegel.title: DDR-Bürgerrechtler blicken zurück: Einig gegen die Diktatur, entzweit über die Demokratie
spiegel.description: Sie bekämpften das SED-Regime und forderten Freiheit. Hier ziehen Akteure der Friedlichen Revolution Bilanz. Und streiten darüber, wer das Erbe von 1989 bedroht – die AfD oder die anderen Parteien.

spiegel.title: Stray Kids schließen sich Grammy-Boykott von BTS an
spiegel.description: Bei den Grammys soll eine neue Kategorie kommen, die so umstritten ist, dass BTS bereits ihr Fernbleiben ankündigten. Nun schließt sich mit den Stray Kids eine weitere K-Pop-Band an.

spiegel.title: AfD-Verbotsverfahren: Hessischer Prüf-Erlass nach Aufruf sorgt für Unruhe in der Justiz
spiegel.description: Ein interner Erlass aus Hessen sorgt für Unruhe unter Juristinnen und Juristen.

spiegel.title: Das E-Auto als Powerbank – jetzt geht es richtig los
spiegel.description: Seit Anfang Oktober gelten für das Laden von Elektroautos neue Regeln – sie haben revolutionäres Potenzial: Millionen Speicher könnten künftig das Stromnetz stabilisieren, wenn Wind und Sonne fehlen.

spiegel.title: Galeria: Warum ein Handelsexperte trotz Pleite noch ans Kaufhaus glaubt
spiegel.description: Der Warenhauskonzern Galeria ist zum vierten Mal pleite. Handelsexperte Carsten Kortum über zu viele Eigentümer, zu wenig Profil – und warum er trotzdem an das Konzept Kaufhaus glaubt.

spiegel.title: Cornell University: Fall Jane Doe rückt Serien sexueller Übergriffe in den Fokus
spiegel.description: Die angezeigte Gruppenvergewaltigung einer Studentin wühlt die Cornell University auf, auch weil hier viele Übergriffe geschehen. Weil es im New Yorker Sexualstrafrecht eine Lücke gibt, könnten Täter zudem straffrei bleiben.

spiegel.title: Oktoberfest: Macht KI-Slop die Wiesn kaputt?
spiegel.description: Das Oktoberfest lebt von Traditionen. Doch in diesem Jahr sorgte ein KI-Verdacht für einen Eklat. Für Münchner Kreative steht mehr auf dem Spiel als guter Geschmack. Eine Ortsbegehung.

spiegel.title: Flydubai-Copilot galt bei Oman Air offenbar als Sicherheitsrisiko
spiegel.description: Der Mann, der einen Flydubai-Flug wohl zum Absturz bringen wollte, wurde offenbar schon bei einem früheren Arbeitgeber auffällig – und suspendiert. Die Ermittler gaben zudem nun bekannt: Die Attacke geschah mit einer Axt.

spiegel.title: John Galliano für Zara: Darf ein Mann, der Hitler liebte, jetzt für Zara Mode machen?
spiegel.description: 15 Jahre nach seinem großen Skandal entwirft John Galliano nun Kleidung für einen Moderiesen. Seine erste Kollektion zeigt, wie viel vom alten Skandaldesigner in den neuen Teilen steckt.

spiegel.title: Michael J. Fox: Schauspieler erhält hohe Auszeichnung in Kanada
spiegel.description: Mit »Zurück in die Zukunft« wurde Michael J. Fox zum Filmstar. Doch der Schauspieler leidet seit Langem an einer schweren Krankheit. Für seinen Einsatz gegen Parkinson wird er in seiner Heimat nun ausgezeichnet.

spiegel.title: Alloparenting: Unerfüllter Kinderwunsch? Ich habe eine verrückte Idee
spiegel.description: Während die einen für den Traum vom eigenen Kind an medizinische, ethische und finanzielle Grenzen gehen, brechen die anderen unter der Last der Care-Arbeit schier zusammen. Dabei gäbe es eine naheliegende Lösung.

spiegel.title: Pornografie: Wie Pornos die Sexualität von Teenagern beeinflussen
spiegel.description: Kinder und Jugendliche sind früh Pornografie ausgesetzt – oft ohne ihr eigenes Zutun. Wie sich die Bilder auf ihre eigene Sexualität auswirken und was Eltern tun können.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: Streit über Justizeingriff in TV-Debatte vor Lula-Bolsonaro-Wahl

phys-org.title: Why tenants choose to move out in connection with renovation
phys-org.description: One in three tenants who moved out of a municipal rental apartment in Gothenburg in connection with renovation said the renovation was a main reason for their decision, and many of them moved out even before construction began. A new study from Chalmers University of Technology shows that concerns about disruption, uncertainty and unclear information can be just as important as rent increases.

phys-org.title: Team selected for NASA program to explore potential lunar cave
phys-org.description: NASA has selected a Planetary Science Institute–led proposal to investigate whether a potentially large underground cave extends beyond the opening of a lunar pit. Such a cave may one day provide a safe haven for astronauts to escape the radiation and extreme temperature swings present at the lunar surface.

phys-org.title: Changes to platinum surface chemistry boost solar hydrogen production in organic photocatalysts
phys-org.description: Researchers from the LIMNO laboratory at EPFL have uncovered how different halides modify the surface chemistry of organic semiconductor nanoparticle photocatalysts. By controlling these phenomena, they have significantly improved the solar hydrogen production efficiency of these materials.

phys-org.title: Researchers turn America's scattered local laws into a free searchable database covering all 50 states
phys-org.description: America is a nation of local laws—millions of them. From noise ordinances and construction codes to rules about fishing licenses and roadside mango peddling, every town, city and county has its own set of regulations and unique way of doing things.

phys-org.title: Marine biologists discover new plankton off Oregon coast
phys-org.description: Nearly every morning when she was a doctoral student in the College of Arts and Sciences (CAS), Nicole Nakata, Ph.D. '23 (biology), would cross the street from the Oregon Institute of Marine Biology (OIMB) in Charleston, Ore., to the high-tide line of the Pacific Ocean. Her job was to catch microscopic brittle star plankton larvae from the incoming tidal current and bring them back to OIMB's labs to analyze under a microscope.

phys-org.title: Mowing less, spraying smarter give pollinators a boost
phys-org.description: Roadsides may not look like wildlife habitat, but a few simple changes to how they are maintained could turn them into much better places for pollinators. A new uOttawa-led study found that reducing mowing and herbicide use along rural roadsides led to a 45% jump in pollinator numbers and a 23% increase in the number of species found there.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover first type I superconductor that breaks time-reversal symmetry
phys-org.description: Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with no resistance and expel magnetic fields when cooled to ultralow temperatures. And depending on their quantum structure, they can also showcase strange properties like magnetic levitation. But now things are getting a little weirder.

phys-org.title: On complex political issues, most Americans take shortcuts to simplicity
phys-org.description: A core assumption in any democracy is that citizens with access to information will make reasoned decisions on political candidates and policy issues. But a new study by UC Berkeley social scientists finds that Americans usually don't consider the full scope of difficult issues, instead basing their opinions on mental shortcuts that sidestep complexity.

phys-org.title: American beech trees may carry genetic resistance to deadly leaf disease
phys-org.description: A study led by scientists at the Holden Arboretum has found evidence that beech leaf disease (BLD) symptom development is genetically controlled, providing the first evidence that some American beech trees may have genetic resistance. This finding supports further investigation and development of breeding populations for BLD resistance. Nearly a third of beech trees near BLD's epicenter in northeastern Ohio, the majority of which were smaller trees, have died since the disease was discovere

phys-org.title: Plasma-activated water tests show concentration matters for effective bacterial disinfection
phys-org.description: In a study published in npj Clean Water, researchers from EPFL investigated how Escherichia coli responds to different concentrations of plasma-activated water (PAW) under nutrient-rich conditions. The team combined conventional colony-forming unit (CFU) counting with nanomotion sensing, a technique that detects nanoscale oscillations produced by metabolically active bacteria.

phys-org.title: Ultrafast X-rays reveal how the light-responsive molecular switch azobenzene changes shape
phys-org.description: Azobenzene is one of the best-known molecules that can be switched between two forms by light. However, the question of how the molecule moves in the first few picoseconds (trillionths of a second) after it absorbs light has remained unresolved for nearly 50 years.

phys-org.title: Why a food poisoning bacterium can cause severe wound infections
phys-org.description: The toxin NheABC, produced by Bacillus cereus, is particularly active in the pH conditions found in open wounds. Researchers at Umeå University found that the toxin damages both cell membranes and mitochondria and helps the bacterium establish infection in wounded tissue.

phys-org.title: Motivation matters more than working memory for improving student math skills, study finds
phys-org.description: Why do some students become ever better at mathematics, while others plateau? Many people may think that mathematics is primarily about cognitive skills. A new study from the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) provides a more nuanced view. The paper is published in the journal Contemporary Educational Psychology.

phys-org.title: Computer-designed protein targets immune receptor linked to inflammation at new 'undruggable' site
phys-org.description: To sense their environment and respond accordingly, cells enlist membrane proteins as communication hubs, receiving molecular messages from outside and triggering responses inside. One of these proteins is Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), an immune receptor that plays an essential role in protecting against infections. But overactivity of TLR4 has been linked to inflammatory disorders like sepsis, arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease, making it an attractive target for therapies. Despite its app

phys-org.title: Small changes can have a big impact on sustainability transitions
phys-org.description: In her dissertation, Hanna Entsalo examines how public policies, such as policy strategies and legislation, influence transitions toward the circular economy and sustainability. Entsalo works as a researcher in the Circular Economy Solutions Unit at the Finnish Environment Institute. Her work focuses on circular economy policy instruments, sustainability transitions and innovation policy, particularly at the national and EU levels.

phys-org.title: Black holes may grow quietly alongside galaxies even without violent mergers
phys-org.description: Astronomers analyzed 2,435 galaxies hosting actively feeding black holes using data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Among them, they identified 546 "bulgeless" galaxies—systems with little or no central stellar bulge. Their paper, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, suggests that galaxies without a central bulge grow black holes just as effectively as galaxies that have one—a surprising sign that black holes don't need galaxy mergers to grow

phys-org.title: Scientists zero in on tiny particles to improve weather and air quality forecasts
phys-org.description: Aerosols are small particles suspended in our atmosphere. They come in many flavors: Wildfire smoke, pollen, desert dust, sea salt lofted by powerful storms, volcanic sulfates and emissions from engines and industrial processes are all examples.

phys-org.title: How does interdisciplinary collaboration work in practice? Three takeaways for teachers
phys-org.description: When we speak with Luyao Huang, her Ph.D. project at Leiden University is in full swing. Two papers—a systematic literature review and a case study on an interdisciplinary course—are already behind her. Next year, she will carry out a study in which teachers react to various scenarios. Today, Huang tells us about her most recent study: a deep dive into student collaboration.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

proj-syn.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
proj-syn.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

proj-syn.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
proj-syn.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

proj-syn.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
proj-syn.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

proj-syn.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

proj-syn.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
proj-syn.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

proj-syn.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
proj-syn.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

proj-syn.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
proj-syn.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.
